JLPT N5 Guide: Format, Scores and a Practical Study Plan

Kanjidon Team · Jan 30, 2026

JLPT N5 is the entry level of the Japanese-Language Proficiency Test. It assesses whether you can understand some basic Japanese through vocabulary, grammar, reading and listening questions. It does not directly test speaking or handwriting. Passing requires both an overall scaled score and minimum scores in each scoring section, so balanced preparation matters more than memorising one unofficial list.

Official N5 Test Format

Timed test sectionOfficial timeWhat it includes
Language Knowledge (Vocabulary)20 minutesKanji readings, orthography, word formation and vocabulary in context
Language Knowledge (Grammar) and Reading40 minutesGrammar forms, sentence composition and short reading tasks
Listening30 minutesTask-based comprehension, key points, verbal expressions and quick responses

The timed test sections above are not identical to the scoring sections. For N5 results, vocabulary, grammar and reading are combined into one 0–120 scoring section; listening is a separate 0–60 scoring section.

Official N5 Pass Marks

RequirementMinimum
Overall score80 out of 180
Language Knowledge and Reading38 out of 120
Listening19 out of 60

You must meet all three requirements. A strong combined language-knowledge and reading score cannot compensate for listening below 19, and the reverse is also true. The JLPT uses scaled scores rather than adding one point for every correct response.

There Is No Official Kanji Syllabus

The JLPT stopped publishing fixed Test Content Specifications after the 2010 revision. A beginner list can organise useful words, but no third-party list defines the current N5 boundary. Check whether you can read those words in official-format questions and short texts.

What to Study

Vocabulary and Kanji in Words

Learn a character through common words and their readings. 日 alone has many possibilities; 日本, 日曜日 and 毎日 provide specific targets. Practise moving in both directions: word to meaning and meaning or sound to the written word.

Grammar and Short Reading

Build core sentence patterns, particles, verb and adjective forms, counters, time expressions and question structures. Then read notices, messages and short passages without translating every word. Identify who, when, where and what action is required.

Listening from the Beginning

Use short basic conversations and practise identifying the task, speaker intention and key detail without replay. Check the transcript after the first attempt, learn the missed language, then listen again.

A Four-Phase Study Plan

PhaseFocusExit check
1. DiagnoseOfficial sample questions and core gapsYou know whether vocabulary, grammar, reading or listening is weakest
2. BuildHigh-utility words, beginner grammar and short audioYou can retrieve core material without relying on answer recognition
3. IntegrateShort reading and listening sets under light time pressureYou can apply the language outside isolated cards
4. RehearseFresh official-format practice under current test timesYou finish sections and meet both overall and sectional targets consistently

The length of each phase depends on your baseline and weekly capacity. This is a sequence, not a promise that N5 takes a fixed number of months.

Exam-Day Checks

  • Read the local test guide and test voucher; reporting times and permitted items vary by host.
  • Bring the exact identification and stationery required by your test site.
  • Plan transport with extra time and confirm the venue before test day.
  • Answer every section; missing an entire required section prevents a pass determination.
  • Use the official section times during practice so pacing is familiar.

Official Sources

  • Official JLPT test sections, question composition and times
  • Official JLPT scoring sections and pass marks
  • Official JLPT FAQ: scaled scores and content lists
  • Official JLPT sample questions and practice workbooks
